authorities.title: SP 330 - Section 2
locators: Table 4, magnetic flux and magnetic flux density rows
observed: The contemporary SI fixes defining constants while retaining the useful base/derived-unit distinction.
Coherent derived units are products of powers of base units with no additional numerical scale factor.
The magnetic-flux row names the weber, symbol Wb, with base-unit expression kg m2 s-2 A-1.
The magnetic-flux-density row names the tesla, symbol T, with base-unit expression kg s-2 A-1.
authorities.use: Confirms the current quantity/unit names and the square-area relationship. The unit identities are exact coherent-unit relationships, not an empirical approximation or a claim that Faraday's experiment replaces the present SI defining constants.

authorities.title: University Physics Volume 2, 13.1 Faraday's Law
locators: Explanation of sign and an open surface bounded by the circuit
SI weber/tesla relationship immediately before the multi-turn discussion
observed: Magnetic flux is the surface integral of the magnetic field's component along the chosen unit normal.
Faraday's law relates induced EMF to the negative time derivative of that flux.
The negative sign concerns the induced-EMF direction.
The surface is bounded by the circuit; a closed circuit does not mean flux through an entire closed surface.
One weber equals one tesla times one square metre; field units may be written as webers per square metre.
authorities.use: Supports the closed-loop one-second weber construction, signed orientation and exact unit relationship. Also supplies the general definition from which the missing uniform-field condition in p0312#5 is independently diagnosed.
authorities.external_example_handling: The case-sensitive terminal-text filter failed to stop at uppercase EXAMPLE13.1, so an external worked example and check-understanding material appeared incidentally in the tool output. authorities.title: SI Units
authorities.observed: The SI has defining constants and coherent derived units. The page routes readers to NIST SP330/SP811.
authorities.use: Background clarification only; not the exact weber/tesla table evidence.

independent_reasoning: The source's unit construction uses a single closed loop. A uniform decrease of its initial flux to zero in one second producing one volt has an initial flux magnitude of one volt-second. This supplies the operational meaning of one weber without introducing a turn-count factor.

The unit construction uses positive magnitudes. The perpendicular condition concerns the field versus the surface plane, not versus the normal; an aligned normal gives the positive product convention. The text is not interpreted as assigning positive signed flux for both possible normals.

Perpendicular orientation does not require the field magnitude to be constant over the surface. The general flux definition sums local normal components; it reduces to the product using one field magnitude and the whole area only when that component is uniform, or when an explicitly defined area average is used. The draft defines no area average and supplies no uniform-field condition.

The surrounding tesla phrase makes terminal1 a numerical value measured in teslas, not a dimensionless magnetic flux density. It is a scientifically sound prose clarification, leaving the raw source and all five original math tokens untouched.
